name: Concord Library

property.ownership_summary: City-owned library parcel; adjoining Civic Center parcel also City-owned

summary: Post-activation rerun confirms the existing area-specific results: ordinary municipal sidewalks, the public entrance/approach, Civic Center walkway, and front public lot are TPF; the ordinary interior remains federally LPF for library-purpose activity; the meeting room is federally LPF. Remaining California interior labels are facility-specific state-constitutional questions rather than statewide qualification gaps.
recording_summary: Recording can constitute First Amendment-protected activity. No dedicated public-facing Concord-specific ordinary-patron camera prohibition was located online. The library-purpose forum classification does not itself create a camera ban; any restriction must be tied to a valid privacy, disruption, safety, or other legal interest and constitutionally tested.

subareas.name: Ordinary lobby, stacks, reading and service areas

federal.note: Library interiors are purpose-limited to reading, research, information access and related library activity; closest ordinary-interior holdings are persuasive rather than Ninth Circuit merits authority.

california.note: No equally close California appellate classification for the full ordinary interior has been established in the pilot record.

recording.summary: LPF status does not itself establish a right to film patrons, screens, staff interactions or private conversations.

subareas.notes: Public access is conditioned by library-purpose and patron-conduct rules.
subareas.unresolved_reason: California Speech Clause treatment of the ordinary interior is not independently hardened. Post-activation rerun confirms this is a facility-specific/local question rather than a statewide California qualification gap.

restriction_audits.summary: Recording can be First Amendment-protected activity in this public-access indoor subarea. No material general recording prohibition is established in the current record; any later claimed restriction must identify its legal source and survive the applicable forum, privacy, and activity-specific constitutional analysis.

indoor_common_space.facility_responsibility: The library retains responsibility for safeguarding patron records, account information, staff systems, and other confidential material under laws and policies that apply to the library.
indoor_common_space.visitor_responsibility: A lawful visitor does not assume the library's confidentiality or information-security duties merely by being present. Any duty imposed on the visitor must come from law or a constitutionally valid rule that applies directly to the visitor.
indoor_common_space.recording_effect: Possible screens, transactions, or private conversations may support targeted restrictions. They do not, by themselves, establish a blanket prohibition on recording the ordinary public interior.

subareas.notes: Faith Center is an unusually close Ninth Circuit / Contra Costa library-room authority.
subareas.unresolved_reason: California Speech Clause label is not necessary to the current federal LPF classification. Post-activation rerun confirms this is a facility-specific/local question rather than a statewide California qualification gap.

restriction_audits.summary: Recording can be First Amendment-protected activity in this public-access indoor subarea. No material general recording prohibition is established in the current record; any later claimed restriction must identify its legal source and survive the applicable forum, privacy, and activity-specific constitutional analysis.

indoor_common_space.facility_responsibility: The library remains responsible for safeguarding protected patron/account information during self-service access and for designing reasonable privacy controls around systems and records.
indoor_common_space.visitor_responsibility: The visitor does not inherit the library's confidentiality duties merely by entering under the self-service access program, although valid agreement terms and independent privacy law can apply directly.
indoor_common_space.recording_effect: The special access agreement and current signs must be checked, but privacy concerns do not automatically convert the self-service interior into a blanket no-camera zone.
